comparison: Both strongly support the three-base probe design claims (C16-C26). OpenEval emphasizes computational evidence from Mfold analysis, while peer reviewers praised the work as 'impressive' with 'high technical quality' and 'clear data.' Both agree on the foundational validity of the approach.

OpenEval supports the Lempel-Ziv complexity analysis (C27-C30) as demonstrating adequate complexity for specific hybridization. Peer reviewers found the complexity index description 'not straightforward to understand' and requested clarification, marking this as UNCERTAIN despite not rejecting the underlying claim.

Both support the single-molecule TIRF/CoSMoS measurements (C31-C33). OpenEval notes appropriate controls and consistency with literature. Peer reviewers stated 'It is clear from the data that their probe design makes the DNA annealing 100 fold faster' with 'high technical quality.'

Both support the mutagenesis experiments demonstrating the three-base rule (C34-C36). OpenEval emphasizes the dose-dependent effect of G residues. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of the clear demonstration that the probe design accelerates annealing 100-fold.

Both support the self-quenching mechanism claims (C37-C38, C58). OpenEval validates the reduced background at high probe concentrations. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these claims through their overall assessment of 'high technical quality' without raising challenges.

Both support the co-localization analysis and promoter-specificity controls (C41-C43). OpenEval notes appropriate controls and interpretation of incomplete template utilization. Peer reviewers accepted these foundational observations without challenge.

OpenEval supports the single-molecule transcription analysis (C44-C47, C86) with multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers marked this UNCERTAIN, stating 'This statement is premature since abortive initiation was not addressed' and suggesting the evidence was incomplete at this stage of the manuscript.

Both support the kinetic measurements and elongation rate calculations (C48-C49). OpenEval validates the linear regression approach. Peer reviewers acknowledged these measurements 'established important benchmarks for future studies,' though noting the T7 RNAP system was well-studied.

Both support the two-color single-molecule experiments and abortive initiation analysis (C50-C54). OpenEval validates the calculation methods. Peer reviewers stated 'the production of the mRNA can be detected with high confidence' and that 'the fastFISH approach was absolutely necessary.'

Both support the specificity controls (C70-C72). OpenEval notes three independent lines of evidence with well-designed controls. Peer reviewers accepted the specificity, stating detection occurs 'with high confidence with minimal false negatives.'

Both support the comparison to literature values and temperature-dependent rate differences (C59-C62, C83). OpenEval notes appropriate citations and reasonable interpretation. Peer reviewers accepted the faster rates as establishing 'important benchmarks' with 'high technical quality.'

OpenEval marks the dwell time estimate (C55) as UNCERTAIN due to large error bars. Peer reviewers support this claim once properly contextualized, requesting citation of known phenomena about polymerase release from DNA ends to avoid 'inventing an ad hoc explanation.'

Both address pausing observations (C63-C64). OpenEval marks C64 as speculative regarding the 'bumping' mechanism. Peer reviewers support these observations without challenge, accepting them as part of the work that 'established important benchmarks for future studies.'

OpenEval supports the high labeling efficiency claim (C87) based on SDS-PAGE analysis. Peer reviewers mark this UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification that T7RNAP is a fusion protein and additional controls for the N-terminal tag's potential effects.

OpenEval supports the established knowledge about secondary structure and hybridization (C18-C20). Peer reviewers found the discussion 'confusing' and 'possibly just mis-written,' noting it 'does not do a great job of separating the discussion of rate-limiting effects.'

OpenEval marks potential applications (C65-C67, C79-C82) as UNCERTAIN, noting they represent future directions rather than demonstrated results. Peer reviewers support these claims, stating the method 'will have a broad appeal' and 'will be useful' for various applications.

Both support the main achievement claims (C5-C7). OpenEval notes these integrate multiple specific findings. Peer reviewers described this as 'an outstanding paper' and emphasized 'the fastFISH approach was absolutely necessary for this work.'

OpenEval supports the explanation for incomplete detection efficiency (C73) based on dark fluorophores and stochastic hybridization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.
OpenEval supports background claims about transcription (C1-C3, C8-C11) as established knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval supports the summary of prior work (C12-C15) establishing motivation for fastFISH. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these motivational claims.
OpenEval supports citations to previous literature providing context (C39-C40, C74-C75). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though C75 appears in peer R8 with different focus.
OpenEval marks claim C57 as UNCERTAIN due to 'data not shown.' No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific observation.

OpenEval marks concerns about probe design and PNA probes (C76-C78) as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable considerations but lacking rigorous experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval supports the calculation of expected elongation time (C69) based on template geometry and literature rates. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this calculation.
